destinations.heroSubtitleAbha: One visit is never enough with all the activities and experiences on offer.
destinations.introBody: On the Sarawat peaks in southwest Saudi Arabia, Abha rests like a jewel crowned in mist and beauty, wrapped in cloud summer and winter.
destinations.introP1: On the Sarawat peaks in southwest Saudi Arabia, Abha rests like a jewel crowned in mist and beauty, wrapped in cloud summer and winter. It is the bright gateway to Aseer and rich with diversity in every direction. Its cool, rainy summers have made it a leading sustainable destination, backed by deep cultural, artistic and heritage assets.
destinations.introP2: Historic fortresses tell centuries of stories—from Shamsan and Dhara to the great and small Daql forts. Heritage museums in restored homes, such as Fatima Museum and Al-Raqidi Museum, introduce visitors to Aseer's treasures.
destinations.introP3: Along Abha Valley runs one of its most famous folk markets, Tuesday Market, beside the artistic Al-Muftaha village—home to arts and the legacy of Talal Maddah.
destinations.introP4: Green fields across Abha supply flowers, grains, fruit and vegetables; locals work in trade, industry and agriculture.
destinations.introP5: Ancient yet calm as a summer dream, Abha competes globally in modern services, dining, cafés, entertainment, sport and year-round festivals and forums.
destinations.introP6: Abha—a treasure whose richness never ends and whose wonder never fades.

attractionsPage.title: Attractions
attractionsPage.subtitle: One visit is never enough with all the activities and experiences on offer.
attractionsPage.introBody: Aseer's historic and cultural landmarks blend authenticity with natural beauty.
attractionsPage.innerIntroP1: Al Abu Sirah palaces rise above the tranquil village of Al-Azizah among the villages of Al-Soudah, bringing together centuries of heritage and a sense of place you will not find elsewhere. The ensemble is made up of three adjacent fortified palaces, each with its own name and symbolism—reflected across dozens of rooms and more than thirty-two chambers where meaning follows naming in authentic Aseeri tradition. A shared eastern balcony on the fourth floor links two of the palaces, opening onto green farmland and towering peaks.
attractionsPage.innerIntroP2: The fortresses were built from mountain stone with thick protective walls engineered to endure raids and harsh weather. Clever layouts made them sanctuaries in peacetime and strongholds in conflict, crowned by a single grand gate that unifies the complex with quiet majesty.
attractionsPage.innerIntroP3: For visitors, Al Abu Sirah is a standout cultural landmark: QR trails at chamber entrances deepen the storytelling, exhibitions and intimate displays bring crafts and arts to life, and seasonal performances fill the courtyards. Pause for coffee beside the palaces or share a memorable meal amid calm mountain air.

1.question: What does Aseer offer as a tourism destination?
1.answer: Aseer is one of Saudi Arabia’s standout regions, with varied landscapes—mountains, plains, wadis and coastlines—and different weather across seasons. It blends heritage architecture, festivals, modern urban hubs and cultural experiences across food, arts and fashion, with accommodation for many budgets and activities year-round.

2.question: When is the best time to visit Aseer?
2.answer: Spring and summer bring milder weather in the highlands plus lively events. Winter can be cool and misty in the mountains; autumn often offers calm hiking conditions.

3.question: What should I pack for Aseer?
3.answer: Pack layers for shifts between coast and mountains, comfortable shoes, sun protection and ID. Check any extra requirements for festivals or sites you plan to visit.

dishesSection.title: Taste traditional Aseeri dishes
dishesSection.description: Aseeri cooking brings mountains, valleys, and farms together on one table: coffee from highland beans, dates from Bisha, mountain wheat and valley grains, fresh dairy, and wildflower honey—often finishing with slow-cooked haneeth from local herds. Explore dishes like haneeth, areekah, mashgothah, asidah, mifa bread from the tannur, marqoush bread, mabthoothah, and more.
